text:
liam: Quick idea — proposing a smoothing-based min-on-demand curve for mixed pools instead of a fixed floor. want feedback before I prototype.
anya: curious, how is smoothing different from just setting min_on_demand=20%?
liam: fixed floors cause cost shocks when spot supply flaps. smoothing raises on-demand gradually as spot availability drops, instead of jumping.
kevin: can you sketch the math? i worry about oscillation and autoscaler thrash.
liam: simple version: target_on_demand = base_floor + slope * max(0, smoothed_spot_shortage). where smoothed_spot_shortage is a moving avg of (demand - spot_capacity)/demand.
sam: so slope is like sensitivity. any caps? we should clamp to [base_floor, max_od]
liam: yep clamp at max_od (e.g., 75%). also a cooldown window to avoid flip-flopping.
marisol: we need to account for regional differences. spot churn in eu-west is way higher than us-west1.
kevin: agree. per-region smoothing params make sense. also add a min_scale_step to prevent tiny scaling operations.
liam: added idea: add a small "burst" pool for transient spikes that uses short-lived preemptible instances with a rapid warm-up bootstrap image. bursts are billed as spot but isolated so we can evict them fast.
anya: how do we handle interruption of the burst pool? some jobs hold large KV cache that would be lost.
liam: two strategies: 1) for latency-critical work, fall back to right-sized on-demand shards with smaller model variants; 2) for long-running batches, checkpoint to durable cache (s3/redis-on-disk) and retry on re-queue.
kevin: fallback to smaller model variant is nice — less cost during eviction and keeps tail latency bounded.
sam: ops-bot has a sim for interruptions right? can we run it on recent usage patterns?
ops-bot: run-sim triggered by liam at 1881234600 — simulation queued. :gear:
liam: sample config idea:
``` 
mixed_pool:
  base_floor_pct: 10
  max_on_demand_pct: 70
  slope: 1.5
  smoothing_window_s: 300
  cooldown_s: 180
  burst_pool:
    enabled: true
    max_pct: 20
    warm_images: ["fast-bootstrap-v2"]
    eviction_strategy: "fallback-on-demand"
```
marisol: can we add a warm-standby of tiny on-demand nodes (1-2 GPUs) per AZ as bootstrapping seeds? saves tens of seconds on cold-spawn.
liam: yes — warm_seeds per-az, with a small memory footprint process that can accept KV warmstarts.
anya: cost-estimate? this sounds like extra on-demand across regions.
kevin: rough calc: base_floor 10% + seeds ~1.5% => <12% on-demand steady. spikes handled by slope and burst. should be cheaper than a 20% fixed floor with equivalent SLAs.
sam: observability — we need per-pool SLOs and a dashboard: spot_availability, smoothed_shortage, on_demand_target_pct, actual_od_pct, churn_rate, eviction_count.
liam: agreed. also add an alert when smoothing drives on-demand > X% for Y minutes.
marisol: migration plan? roll this as opt-in to canary tenant groups, run sim for 2 weeks, then ramp.
liam: plan: 1) sim + bench in staging 2) canary on low-traffic customers 3) measure cost and p99 latency 4) iterate.
kevin: we should also test network-constrained AZ scenarios (e.g., limited GCE spare capacity) — smoothing could mask real infra failures.
san: (typo) ^sam
sam: also: add a safety net — if spot_revocations > threshold, hard-fallback to reserved on-demand pool and notify.
liam: thanks — i'll prototype a controller that reads spot metrics and outputs target_on_demand_pct per-region + commands to autoscaler.
anya: ok for me. :+1:
kevin: let's sync tomorrow in 1p to review metrics and sim output.
liam: thanks everyone. tagging follow-ups: @marisol you own warm-seed design, @kevin you own alert thresholds, @anya you own sim scenarios.
